text:
One year ago, I started this company with a pitch deck, too much coffee and a lot of confidence.

Here's what year one actually looked like:

→ $180k in revenue
→ A team of 4
→ 2 failed pivots
→ 17 paying customers in month 11

The number I think about most is the 2 failed pivots.

Both times, I was sure we'd found it. Both times, the market told us otherwise. At first those pivots felt like failures. Looking back, they were the most expensive and most useful lessons we had all year. Each one taught us what customers don't need, and that made what they do need easier to see.

Some other things I learned:

• Small teams move fast when everyone owns the outcome. I couldn't ask for better people than these 3.
• Revenue is honest feedback. Compliments are easy to give. Paying is a real commitment.
• Hitting 17 paying customers in month 11 meant more to me than any metric on a slide. Real people chose us.

Year one humbled me. Year two, we build on what's working.

To everyone who believed early, thank you. We're just getting started.
